task.description:
Design the fix for GH-595 / ISS-0628 (MINOR -- does not block LUA-16's release): ScriptErrorPayload.stack_trace is always empty for real LuaJIT 2.1 runtime errors because src/lua/executor.zig's lua_pcall call (line ~543: `bindings.lua_pcall(L, 0, 1, 0)`) passes errfunc=0. By the time captureStackTrace runs (line ~585, AFTER lua_pcall returns), the erroring Lua call frames have already unwound, so lua_getstack(level=0) returns 0.

CONFIRMED DIAGNOSIS (ISSUE-FIXER, WF03-GH595-20260809 Step 1, verified against current main source directly, not just the issue text):

1. lua_pcall message-handler mechanism (Lua Reference Manual, Lua 5.1 / LuaJIT 2.1 API): a message handler, if used, must be PUSHED ONTO THE STACK BEFORE the function-to-be-called (and its arguments); its absolute stack index is passed as lua_pcall's 4th argument (errfunc). If errfunc is 0, no handler is installed (today's state). If installed, the handler is invoked with the raw error object as its argument AT THE MOMENT the error is raised -- while the offending call frames are STILL LIVE -- and its return value becomes the final error object lua_pcall returns to the caller. This is the mechanism the fix must route captureStackTrace's walk through, instead of calling it standalone after lua_pcall has already returned.

2. captureStackTrace itself (executor.zig:701, lua_getstack/lua_getinfo walk) is NOT buggy and must NOT be rewritten -- only WHEN it is invoked needs to change. TC-ISS-0625-LUA-16-02 (src/lua/iss0625_lua_12_15_16_test.zig ~L272) correctly tests that it returns empty on an idle stack (no active call) and must keep passing unchanged after this fix.

3. CRITICAL CORRECTION vs. GH-595's own filed issue text and vs. a comment already embedded in tests/integration/iss0625_lua_12_15_16_test.zig (~L561-566): both suggest installing Lua's own `debug.traceback` as the errfunc. THIS IS NOT VIABLE AS FILED. src/lua/stdlib.zig's loadSafeStdlib (invariant SBX-1, documented at the file's own header: 'Never opened: io, os, package, debug, jit, ffi, bit, coroutine') never calls luaopen_debug. The debug library is deliberately and permanently absent from the sandboxed Lua state for security reasons -- src/lua/host_context.zig's registry-channel design relies on `debug` being unreachable to scripts. `debug.traceback` is therefore not a lookupable global inside the sandbox (lua_getglobal(L, "debug") would push nil). The design MUST NOT propose opening the debug library, even partially, to get this working.

4. RECOMMENDED FIX SHAPE: a small internal `lua_CFunction` closure (installed via `bindings.lua_pushcclosure`, already bound at luajit_bindings.zig:134) that, when invoked as the message handler, runs the SAME lua_getstack/lua_getinfo walk captureStackTrace already implements (either by factoring that walk into a shared helper callable from both places, or by having the closure call captureStackTrace directly with the still-live `L`) and pushes the resulting string as its return value (or leaves it in a location the outer Zig code can retrieve after lua_pcall returns, e.g. registry storage -- design should pick one and justify it, since a lua_CFunction callback signature is `fn(L) c_int` and does not have direct access to the outer Zig context.allocator without going through the registry channel host_context.zig already uses for other cross-boundary state). No new luajit_bindings.zig symbols are required: lua_pushcclosure (line 134) and lua_getglobal (line 228) are already bound; lua_pcall's binding (line 169) already accepts errfunc as a parameter -- only the call site's hardcoded 0 (executor.zig:543) needs to become the handler's absolute stack index.

5. Required call-site restructuring at executor.zig ~L512-543: currently `luaL_loadbuffer` pushes the compiled chunk directly onto a stack that has nothing else on it, then `lua_pcall(L, 0, 1, 0)` is called. The fix must push the handler closure FIRST (before luaL_loadbuffer's chunk), note its absolute stack index (use lua_gettop, not a relative/negative index, since the design must document precisely why -- relative indices shift as more values are pushed), then push/load the chunk, then call `lua_pcall(L, 0, 1, handler_index)`. Design must also specify how the handler's captured trace crosses back into the existing post-pcall code path (line ~585's `captureStackTrace(L, context.allocator) catch ""` call either needs to be replaced entirely with 'read what the handler already computed', or the handler needs to leave the state such that the existing captureStackTrace call still works -- pick one, the former is likely cleaner since after lua_pcall returns with a handler installed, the ERROR OBJECT ON THE STACK is now whatever the handler returned, not the raw error string, which also affects err_msg extraction at line 545 `bindings.lua_tostring(L, -1)` -- the design must specify how error_message and stack_trace are BOTH still recovered correctly post-call, e.g. handler returns a table {message=..., trace=...} or a delimited string the Zig side parses, or the handler stashes the trace via a registry key while returning the original message unchanged so err_msg extraction at line 545 is untouched).

6. LUA-15 (explicit failure) interaction: host_context.readExplicitFailure (called at line 555, AFTER the pcall) is unaffected -- it reads the registry discriminator LUA-15 already writes, unrelated to the errfunc mechanism. Explicit failures still skip stack-trace capture entirely per current logic (view.kind == .Explicit branch, no captureStackTrace call). Design should confirm this branch needs zero changes.

7. INSTRUCTION LIMITER / MEMORY LIMITER / WATCHDOG INTERACTION (checked, not assumed) -- from GH-495/PR#593, same session:
   a. MemoryLimiter.alloc (wired via lua_newstate) is orthogonal: it only intercepts allocation calls, never touches the pcall error path. No interaction.
   b. The LUA-10 watchdog (timeout.zig WatchdogState/WatchdogHandle) runs on a SEPARATE std.Thread that never calls any lua_* function and never touches L directly (confirmed via timeout.zig's own docstring: 'never touches L and never calls any lua_* function... lua_error's longjmp must run on the thread that owns the state'). It only sets a flag the in-VM count hook polls. Zero direct interaction with the errfunc mechanism.
   c. The LUA-08/LUA-10 combined count hook (instruction_limiter.zig hookCallback, installed via lua_sethook/LUA_MASKCOUNT) DOES interact: when it trips (instruction limit or wall-clock timeout exceeded), raiseLimit() calls lua_pushstring + lua_error(L) -- lua_error is the SAME longjmp-based unwind a genuine script runtime error uses, and it unwinds through the nearest enclosing lua_pcall exactly like any other error. CONSEQUENCE: once an errfunc is installed, limiter-triggered errors will ALSO now invoke the new message handler and produce a captured stack trace -- not just organic script bugs. This is not a conflict, but it IS an observable behavior change beyond GH-595's literal ask (limiter-triggered ScriptErrorPayloads currently also get empty stack_trace; after this fix they likely will not). Design MUST state explicitly whether this is accepted as in-scope bonus diagnostic value (recommended -- more trace data on limiter trips is strictly useful for debugging runaway scripts) or whether it needs special-casing to preserve today's empty-trace behavior for limiter-triggered errors specifically. Check tests/integration and src/lua unit tests for any limiter test that currently asserts stack_trace.len == 0 on a limiter-triggered error -- if one exists, it will need the same assertion flip as TC-ISS-0625-LUA-16-int-01, or an explicit carve-out.

Full diagnosis and acceptance criteria are also recorded in docs/issues/ISS-0628.json.

DO NOT IMPLEMENT. Produce the Type E prose design artefact at src/design/ per backend_developer_guide.md §6, then route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR.
acceptance_criteria: Design specifies the exact message-handler closure shape (lua_CFunction via lua_pushcclosure) and confirms it does NOT rely on debug.traceback or opening the debug library
Design specifies exact stack push ordering and how the handler's absolute index is computed and passed as lua_pcall's errfunc argument

Design specifies precisely how error_message (currently read via lua_tostring(L,-1) after pcall) and stack_trace (currently read via captureStackTrace after pcall) are both correctly recovered once a handler transforms the top-of-stack error object
Design confirms TC-ISS-0625-LUA-16-02 (idle-stack unit test) requires no changes
Design specifies the required flip of TC-ISS-0625-LUA-16-int-01's final assertion (== 0 to > 0) and correction of its stale comments/title referencing debug.traceback

Design explicitly resolves the instruction-limiter/watchdog interaction question (accept broader trace capture on limiter trips, or special-case it) and checks for any existing test asserting empty trace on a limiter-triggered error
Design confirms the LUA-15 explicit-failure branch needs no changes
No implementation code written by CODE-DESIGNER -- prose design only, Type E per templates/lego-catalog.md
